liam: Quick notewe're seeing a tail allocation latency pattern that looks related to coalesce kicking in during tight microbatch windows. Wanted to brainstorm an adaptive heuristic.

anika: What's the concrete signal? Is it p99 alloc time or minor pagefault bursts?

liam: p99 alloc spikes (~6-12ms) and a small uplift in minor faults from /proc/vmstat correlated with coalesce runs. Not every tenant, mostly medium-tenants with mixed small/medium frees.

pete: Could be that a static coalesce_interval is misaligned with tenant activity. We should make coalesce rate tenant-aware: lower frequency when alloc_rate high.

anika: Agreed. Proposal: compute a simple activity score per-tenant over 30s window = allocs_per_sec * avg_free_ratio. Map score to mode: 0->conservative, mid->balanced, high->defer.

liam: For defer mode, we stop background coalesce and instead encourage opportunistic local merges on free fastpath (if implemented). That reduces contention.

pete: Also add jitter to coalesce start times to avoid global synchronized storms across tenants. Even a few hundred ms random jitter helps.

anika: We need to be careful with eviction interactions: deferring coalesce may increase fragmentation and trigger earlier NVMe spills. How do we detect that tradeoff?

liam: Metric pair to track: coalesce_savings_rate (free_range_reduction/sec) vs spill_rate_change. If after X minutes spill_rate rises > threshold, flip tenant back to balanced automatically.

pete: That implies a feedback controller: trial a deferred period T, observe spill delta, revert if negative. Keep conservative safe default for Hosted.

anika: API surface: don't expose raw knobs. Expose policy = "auto|balanced|aggressive|off". Auto uses activity score mapping and safety checks. Keep tenant override for Dedicated/Private.

liam: Implementation details: maintain per-tenant counters in allocator shims (lockless ring buffers). Compute activity_score with EWMA to avoid flip-flopping.

pete: Also flag: try_coalesce fast-path should return immediately if it sees recent allocs on the same CPU to avoid stealing caches. Use per-cpu stamp.

anika: For telemetry, we want tenant.activity_score, coalesce_runs, coalesce_time_ms_hist, spill_rate, alloc_p99_pre/post. Console tile should show suggested policy per tenant.

infra-bot: nightly-sim run for adaptive-coalesce scheduled at 1831234575 :gear:

liam: Edge cases: long idle periods then sudden burst: EWMA may be slow to respond and postpone needed coalesce. We should allow burst-triggered emergency coalesce if fragmentation exceeds a threshold (e.g., free_range_count in small bucket > X).

pete: Good point. Emergency coalesce should be limited to a small budget so it won't thrash. Also mark emergency runs in telemetry.

anika: Operational runbook: if tenant sees alloc_p99 > Y and coalesce_fail_trylock increased concurrently, auto-set policy=conservative and notify SRE.

liam: Next steps: I'll prototype the activity score and auto mapping, add the jitter, and run a 2h simulation across mixed tenants. Pete can draft the controller revert rules and thresholds. Anika will sketch the Console UX.

pete: I'll also open a short RFC describing the per-tenant counters and the emergency coalesce budget API.

anika: SGTM. Keep Hosted default to balanced/auto but conservative fail-safes.

liam: Thanks. I'll post simulation logs here when ready.
